Fix statusline displaying double %% signs. The percent literals were in shell variable assignments (not printf format strings), so %% passed through printf %b as two literal % characters.

Add SendMessage to tool lists of all pipeline agents that coordinate via messages: task-executor (19 body refs), project-manager (10), code-review (4), task-tester (4). Only watchdog had it (added in seq 149). Watchdog first-tick STATUS report replaces Lead's direct usage file read. The script now emits {"alert":"STATUS","pct_5h":...,"pct_7d":...} on its first tick, PM forwards to Lead, and Lead waits for this before spawning task teams. Eliminates Lead reading usage-status.json directly (which could hit stale data from idle sessions). Watchdog is now the single source of truth for all usage data. Updated PM, phase-1-setup, spawn prompts, and usage-control reference.

Watchdog script outputs JSON lines instead of plain text. Fixes hallucination bug where Haiku fabricated alerts from Monitor lifecycle notifications (e.g. inventing 'KILL 5h 100' when usage was 4%). Script now emits structured JSON like {"alert":"KILL","window":"5h","pct":96,"resets_at":...} — Haiku checks for JSON with an "alert" field and ignores anything else. Also: added SendMessage to watchdog tool list (was missing — the agent couldn't forward alerts), added debug log (.watchdog-debug.log) that records every tick's readings and account key, simplified check_window with rank-based tier comparison replacing duplicated escalation logic. Updated PM agent and spawn prompts to parse the new JSON format.

Fix Watchdog monitoring wrong account in multi-account setups. The bash script used '.accounts | sort_by(.updated_at) | last' which picked whichever account was most recently written to, not the one running the plan. Now Lead resolves the active account key via 'claude auth status' + slugifyEmail at plan start (new step 1.8), passes ACCOUNT_KEY through the watchdog spawn prompt, and the script uses '.accounts[$key]' for direct lookup. Same fix applied to the pre-task budget assessment and usage-control reference.

Replace CronCreate with Monitor in the Watchdog agent. A self-contained bash monitoring script now does all threshold checking (CONSERVE/PAUSE/KILL for both 5h and 7d windows), stall detection, and data freshness — running every 60 seconds in a persistent Monitor process. The script outputs alert lines ONLY on state transitions; clean ticks produce zero stdout. Monitor delivers each line as a notification to the Haiku model, which simply forwards it to PM via SendMessage. On clean ticks: no stdout → no Monitor notification → model never prompted → zero tokens wasted → zero Lead noise. Previously, CronCreate fired a prompt every minute forcing the model to respond (framework constraint: models can't produce zero tokens), and TeamCreate delivered the response to Lead, burning ~30-60K Opus tokens per 5-hour execution for nothing. The bash script handles: per-window threshold evaluation with escalation (CONSERVE→PAUSE→KILL), USAGE-RESET detection, state file management (.watchdog-state.json), data freshness checks with 10-minute cooldown, stall detection against events.json/plan.json, and stall-ping cleanup for completed tasks.

Replace two-tier usage control (SOFT-LIMIT/HARD-LIMIT) with three-tier CONSERVE/PAUSE/KILL system. CONSERVE (5h ≥80%, 7d ≥90%) stops spawning new teams — no agent messages sent. PAUSE (5h ≥90%, 7d ≥95%) tells all active agents to go idle via text message — idle agents consume zero tokens, full context preserved. KILL (5h ≥95%, 7d ≥98%) force-terminates agents via shutdown_request protocol message — the only mechanism that reliably stops agents. On USAGE RESET: PAUSE recovery sends RESUME to idle agents (instant, zero re-spawn cost); KILL recovery re-spawns teams from checkpoint using per-task files (crash-recovery flow). Lead enters hold state during PAUSE/KILL — defers all ADVICE/QUERY from paused/killed agents to prevent accidentally unblocking stopped work. Watchdog signals renamed throughout (CONSERVE/PAUSE/KILL replace SOFT-LIMIT/HARD-LIMIT). PM forwarding updated to match. All three task-team agents (task-executor, code-review, task-tester) gain explicit PAUSE/RESUME handling and mid-execution shutdown_request approval instructions. Checkpoint template gains Usage State section for recovery. Docs site and help skill updated. Fixes incident where text STOP messages were ignored for 33 minutes while agents continued 8 fix cycles.

On genuinely stalled takes, Executor now escalates via ADVICE REQUEST task-$TASK_ID [knowledge] to Lead and waits for a ruling instead of writing a stub. Reviewer side (agents/code-review.md step 2) tightened to treat take synthesis as critical-path work — the Executor is explicitly blocked on this message. Extend plan-execution usage control to monitor BOTH rate-limit windows (5-hour and 7-day) with independent thresholds, and unify Lead's response across windows. New thresholds: 5h soft 80% / hard 90% (was 75/90), 7d soft 90% / hard 95% (new). Watchdog reads both .rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage and .rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage from ~/.claude/ultra/usage-status.json on every tick and applies signal rules independently per window. Signals are now window-qualified: WATCH: SOFT-LIMIT window={5h|7d} pct=X resets_at=Y (same for HARD-LIMIT and USAGE-RESET). The watchdog state file gains per-window last_signal tracking under .five_hour and .seven_day keys — the two windows never suppress each other, so it is expected to see two signals on the same tick when both cross their thresholds simultaneously. PM validates window-qualified signals against the matching window field and forwards to Lead with a [5h] or [7d] label. Lead's behavior is now uniform across windows and encoded in the new shared/lead.md ## Usage Blocks section: on SOFT-LIMIT, active teams finish their current task but no new teams are spawned and a Phase 3 checkpoint fires on the next task done; on HARD-LIMIT, all active teams are stopped immediately via SendMessage STOP messages and a checkpoint fires right away; on USAGE-RESET, only the named window's entry clears, and Lead resumes spawning only when no blocks remain. Pre-task-1 budget assessment now considers both pct_5h and pct_7d — the binding constraint is whichever window runs out first. The 7d reset horizon can be hours or days, so usage-control.md advises Lead to inform the user when entering a 7d hard pause. Operational report gains window-qualified usage-event breakdowns. plugin.json and marketplace.json NOT bumped in this entry — committer must chain the version bump to 2026.04.14-11 after the pending seq 137 commit lands. No project-template files change — migration is null.

Fold the tmux disconnected-session reaper (formerly /uc:session-cleanup) into /uc:setup as an optional, strictly opt-in step backed by a new reference file at skills/setup/references/session-cleanup.md. The standalone skill directory skills/session-cleanup/ is removed along with its help entry and the dedicated row in docs/views/docs/reference.ejs — setup now owns the entire install/repair/remove lifecycle for the reaper. New check 3.11 in setup detects platform (Linux + systemctl), file presence, systemd timer enable/active state, and linger; new fix 5.11 presents the tradeoff explicitly before touching anything. The opt-in prompt in the reference spells out that the reaper CLEANS UP stale tmux sessions but DISRUPTS the ability to resume any detached session older than 24 hours (scrollback and running processes are lost) — users who rely on long-lived detached tmux sessions are told to skip. The setup marker file grows a new checks.sessionCleanup slot with values installed|skipped|not-linux|opted-out. Help skill and docs reference page are updated to mention the new capability on the Setup entry. No project-template files change — the reaper still writes under $HOME only — so migration is null.

Remove the original Ultra session-file cleanup sub-flow from /uc:session-cleanup. The skill is now exclusively the tmux disconnected-session reaper installer from seq 135 — no more Step 0 AskUserQuestion with two paths, no more transcript index, no more `.claude/ultra/sessions/*.json` walking or classification. The file-based method was never reliable in practice: the Ultra session file schema has no `pid`, no `last_activity`, and no tmux linkage, and cross-referencing Claude Code transcript jsonl files for liveness proved fragile (dash-as-slash encoding collisions, bind-mount duplicates, stuck-active files that outlived the transcripts). Keeping the tmux reaper as the only method — it has a precise liveness signal (`session_last_attached` + `session_created` from tmux format vars), runs out-of-band via a user-level systemd timer, and solves the actual pain point for VSCode Remote SSH users. The help skill entry and docs/views/docs/reference.ejs row are updated to describe the single remaining sub-flow. A short note in the skill's Notes section acknowledges the removed session-file method so users re-reading the skill understand why it's gone. The skill frontmatter is tightened: Glob/Grep dropped from allowed-tools (no longer walks projects), argument-hint clarifies the install/repair/remove decision tree. No project-template files change — the skill only writes under $HOME — so migration is null.

Extend the session-cleanup skill with a second sub-flow: an optional tmux disconnected-session reaper for Linux/systemd users. The original Ultra session-file cleanup becomes sub-flow A; the new sub-flow B detects install state, describes the proposed behavior to the user (including a live dump of current tmux sessions and which ones would be killed right now), and on confirmation installs three files — `$HOME/.local/bin/tmux-reap-disconnected.sh`, `$HOME/.config/systemd/user/tmux-reap.service`, and `$HOME/.config/systemd/user/tmux-reap.timer` — then enables the user-level timer and verifies it is active. The reaper uses `session_last_attached` and `session_created` from tmux format vars to compute per-session disconnect age, kills anything detached for more than 24h, and never touches currently-attached sessions. Motivating scenario: VSCode Remote SSH users whose integrated terminals auto-launch tmux end up with tmux sessions piling up on the VM after every window close — this gives them a hands-off, threshold-based cleanup without resorting to `destroy-unattached on` (which wrongly kills sessions on manual Ctrl-b d) or CPU-idle heuristics (which can't distinguish afk-with-claude-code from truly dead). The sub-flow also handles loginctl linger (required so the timer runs when no SSH session is active) and offers repair/reinstall/remove paths for idempotency. Non-Linux platforms skip sub-flow B cleanly. Step 0 now asks which sub-flow(s) to run via AskUserQuestion, so existing callers of the skill that only want session-file cleanup still get it in one click. Help skill entry updated to describe both sub-flows. No project-template files change — the skill installs machine-local systemd units under `$HOME`, not under any project — so migration is null.

Cut idle Watchdog and PM wake-ups to Lead at the source. The Lead wake-up trace from seq 132 immediately caught three noise wake-ups in a single screenshot: two from Watchdog ('task verification — initialized, no alerts' and 'no action needed') and one from PM ('PM ready, plan.json healthy'). None carry actionable content. Watchdog is a Haiku cron agent previously instructed to 'respond with just ok' on clean ticks; that 'ok' text — plus any improvised status word Haiku produces — was leaking to the spawner (Lead) as assistant-turn output, and the stylistic 'Do not message Lead' rule was too weak to stop improvisation. PM was emitting one informational startup ping ('PM initialized — plan.json and events.json ready. Monitoring active.') that Lead has no handler for and never acts on. Edits in agents/watchdog.md: the CronCreate TICK prompt (step 3), the Monitoring Checks preamble, section 4 'Respond', and the 'What NOT to do' list now all require silent turns on clean ticks — no text, no SendMessage, just end the turn. The Lead rule is strengthened from 'Do not message Lead' to 'NEVER SendMessage to Lead under any circumstances; the ONLY allowed recipient is pm-{PLAN_NAME}; even on shutdown you reply in-thread, you do not initiate.' This makes the rule mechanical (single-recipient constraint) instead of stylistic, which Haiku follows better. Edits in agents/project-manager.md: the startup SendMessage to Lead is removed from the startup sequence (step 7) and its mirror bullet is removed from PM's 'You send to Lead' documentation list, so the spec matches the behavior. All validated alert paths stay untouched — PM still forwards USAGE HARD/SOFT-LIMIT, USAGE RESET, STALL, STALE DATA, dashboard URL, escalations, and the operational-report notice, all of which are actionable with matching handler rows in plan-execution. The wake-up trace itself is deliberately kept in place so the user can verify the noise is gone before removing the audit tool; a future plan will remove the trace once silence is confirmed. No project-template files change, so migration is null.

Rewrite /uc:session-cleanup around the actual schema the session-start/session-end hooks produce. Previous version classified by `pid`, `last_activity`, and `tmux_pane` — fields that were documented but never written by any hook, so classification silently defaulted every real file to ENDED/LEGACY and the stuck-active bucket was invisible. Also fixed a lossy project-discovery bug: decoding `~/.claude/projects/` directory names by replacing every dash with a slash drops every project whose name contains a hyphen, so large project trees were missed entirely. The new flow: (1) walk the filesystem with `find $HOME -path '*/.claude/ultra/sessions'` instead of decoding encoded names; (2) build a `session_id → transcript_mtime` index from `$HOME/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` because Claude Code's transcript is the only file that gets appended on every turn — the Ultra session.json is written once at start and once at end, so it is useless as a liveness signal; (3) classify each session file using `started_at` age + transcript-mtime silence against a single user-supplied threshold (default 1 day): young sessions are always kept, old sessions are killed unless their transcript was touched within the threshold, legacy sessions (no `started_at`) are killed unless transcript-active; (4) present a per-project kill plan and delete via a simple `rm` stream over a temp kill-list file. Added a Background section explaining the real schema so future readers don't rebuild the same wrong mental model. Tmux-pane killing removed — the schema never carried a tmux reference. help/SKILL.md entry rewritten to match. Also removes 7 session-state files that had been accidentally tracked in this repo before `.gitignore` started excluding `.claude/ultra/sessions/`.

Plan-execution Lead: replace the 'be silent between messages' rule with a temporary wake-up trace requirement so the user can audit which senders are actually noisy. Background: Lead has been spamming 'Waiting for executor-N' / state-narration text between handler turns. Root cause is structural — Claude's assistant loop must produce either a tool call or text per turn, and rows like FILE-UPDATED ('No Lead action') and pipeline 'planning complete — awaiting implementation approval' ('No reply needed') give Lead nothing to call, so the model fills the empty turn with narration. Prose telling it to 'be silent' can't beat the mechanical constraint. Interim diagnostic fix: every wake-up must produce exactly one sentence describing the message just received (sender + type + task ID), e.g. 'Received: FILE-UPDATED task-3/impl.md from executor-3.' or 'Received: code complete from executor-2.' This is the only allowed per-wake-up text — no commentary, no prediction, no 'waiting for X.' Once the user has reviewed the trace logs, we'll cut the noisy senders at the source (likely: stop CC'ing Lead on FILE-UPDATED broadcasts, drop the pipeline parking confirmation ping) and remove the trace requirement. Edits in skills/plan-execution/SKILL.md: rewrote the Message Handlers preamble (line 113), updated the post-handler return rule (line 138), expanded the Anti-Patterns section to clarify that the trace is the only allowed output and is not a license for narration, and tightened the constraint bullet.

Consolidate Tech Stack sweep rule into the planning framework base (follow-up to seq 130). The previous commit put the mandatory sweep in references/planning-framework/stage-2.md AND duplicated mode-specific expansions in feature-mode and debug-mode stage-2.md — redundant restatements that would drift from the base rule over time. Consolidation: (1) base rule in planning-framework/stage-2.md rewritten to be fully mode-agnostic — 'Every planning mode ... must sweep /uc:research over every core technology the in-scope files will touch,' with the in-scope file set defined as 'whatever the active mode flags as in-scope for this planning session.' (2) mode extensions in feature-mode, debug-mode, and doc-code-verification-mode stage-2.md reduced to one-paragraph notes that name each mode's in-scope file source: feature = draft task breakdown's Files list; debug = files under investigation for the bug; verification = code files in the verification matrix. The mechanical sweep rule, strict derivation, canonicalization note, research-to-task mapping, and downstream effect all live in the base and are inherited by all modes. (3) doc-code-verification-mode gains its Tech Stack sweep note for the first time (wasn't in seq 130).

/uc:research gains canonical slug normalization + pre-flight duplicate prevention, and planning Stage 2 gains a mandatory Tech Stack sweep rule. Closes a regression vs. the old Tech Knowledge agent: when a plan 'just extended existing code using already-known libraries,' the new lazy research flow produced nothing because nothing was new — but the knowledge base also stayed empty, so executors and reviewers still hit cold QUERY round-trips for every library the codebase already uses. Two coordinated changes: (1) In SKILL.md Step 3, a new three-part flow — 3a derives a raw slug from the topic, 3b canonicalizes it by stripping version markers (`v\d+`, `\d+\.\d+`), topic-noise words (api/schema/config/middleware/client/consumer/etc. for library mode, strategies/patterns/approach for patterns mode, competitors/alternatives/trends for market mode), and method-level qualifiers, reducing 'nats jetstream consumer config' → `nats`, 'zod v4 schemas' → `zod`, 'prisma findUnique' → `prisma`. 3c runs a broader pre-flight jq query that matches existing entries whose subject is equal to or a whole-token prefix of the canonical slug (with `sort_by(subject | length)` preferring the shortest canonical home), so different phrasings of the same library always route to the same research file — no duplicates. (2) SKILL.md Step 1 gains a `--fill-only` flag: full flow still runs (classify → canonicalize → cache check → spawn on miss), but the caller's return payload is a compact `{target_path, mode, subject, status: hit|spawned|refreshed|failed, expires}` envelope instead of the H2 section content or agent summary. Designed for bulk sweeps where the caller only needs 'is this research on disk now?' not 'what does it say?' — saves ~2-5K tokens per entry. (3) New 'Tech Stack Sweep — MANDATORY' section in references/planning-framework/stage-2.md with a strict mechanical derivation rule: for every file in the draft Files list, read imports, sweep `/uc:research {lib} --fill-only` per external package. Applies even to libraries the project already uses — the whole point is to fill the knowledge base so execution teams get cache hits instead of cold QUERYs. (4) feature-mode and debug-mode Stage 2 extensions describe how each mode derives its file set for the sweep: feature-mode from the draft task breakdown, debug-mode from the files under investigation for the bug. Research-to-task mapping is tracked during Stage 2 and turned into task.md `**Research:**` pointers at Stage 4 Step 5b, with Lead's pre-spawn coverage check degrading to a rarely-firing safety net because the knowledge base is already populated.

/uc:research: fix silent cache-miss bailouts. The skill had conditional language in Step 6 ('If the index query returned null...') and no top-level invariant enforcing that every invocation produces a result. Agents running the skill could hit ambiguous in-between cases — index returned a fresh-by-date entry whose topics[] didn't actually cover the user's topic, or a weak summary-only match, or classification ambiguity that resolved to 'idk' — and silently return 'no match found' without firing Step 6. Fix: (1) new mandatory Invariant section at the top stating every invocation ends in one of two outcomes — cache hit or agent spawn, no third option; (2) rewrite Step 5 as an explicit three-check list (non-null entry AND topics/subject substring match AND not expired) with explicit fall-through to Step 6 on any miss, including H2-section-not-found-in-file (index claimed coverage the file doesn't deliver); (3) rewrite Step 6 header as 'MANDATORY ON ANY NON-HIT' with an enumerated list of cases that land there; (4) add 'cache miss is the default fallback, not a separate condition' guideline. No behavior change on successful cache hits; the fix closes the 'I checked the cache and nothing was a good match' failure mode where the agent would narrate instead of spawn.

Usage-limit management redesign: replace PM's 5-min cron polling with a three-agent system (Haiku watchdog → PM → Lead). New Haiku watchdog agent ticks every 1 minute checking usage thresholds (75% soft, 90% hard) and executor staleness (>10 min silence), signals PM only when something needs attention. PM becomes event-driven (no cron) — validates watchdog alerts, adds operational context, forwards to Lead with recommendations, tracks per-task budget data (usage % at start/end of each task). Lead is the decision-maker — can decide not to start task 1, stop spawning, pause teams, hard-stop, or resume, guided by new usage-control.md reference. Watchdog placed in PM column in tmux layout. Per-task budget object added to plan.json schema. ~6x token cost reduction for monitoring.

Four small follow-ups to the file-based team context refactor (seq 125). (1) Remove a leftover `shared/knowledge-brief.md` reference from phase-5-completion.md — the brief was deleted from the model in seq 125 but this shutdown-time instruction still told Lead to preserve it. Messages become pure triggers. (3) Normalize path notation in agents/task-executor.md from `tasks/task-{N}/impl.md` to `tasks/task-$TASK_ID/impl.md` — file-system paths use the runtime variable, while operational message templates (`Task {N} done`, `Task {N} escalation needed`) correctly stay on the `{N}` convention because Lead's message handler table matches them literally. (4) Update the anti-pattern list fossil in plan-execution/SKILL.md: `"Plan looks solid." (unless formal APPROVED response to plan review)` → references `ADVICE REQUEST task-N [deviation]` instead, since there is no formal plan-review step anymore.

/uc:research splits cache into two scopes. Product/domain research stays at `documentation/technology/research/` (libraries, patterns) + `documentation/product/research/` (market). Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic API research now lands in a dedicated harness scope at `.claude/ultra/research/{subject}.md` (flat layout, e.g. `claude-code.md`, `claude-agent-sdk.md`, `anthropic-api.md`) with its own `.claude/ultra/research/index.json`. Rationale: Claude knowledge is meta — about the tooling we build *with*, not about the product domain — so it belongs alongside other harness state in `.claude/ultra/`, not under `documentation/technology/research/libraries/` (which implies importable libraries the product depends on). Skill auto-detects Claude/Anthropic topics in Step 2 and routes Step 3 (target path) and Step 4 (index path) to the harness scope. The researcher agent gained scope-aware bootstrap (creates `.claude/ultra/research/` with README + empty index on first Claude lookup), scope-aware index key format (flat for harness, relative-from-research-root for product), and an explicit `rm -f {index_path}.tmp` step in the atomic-write protocol to fix a tmp-file leak observed in testing. library-mode reference notes the dedicated output path; help skill description updated.

File-based Lead↔team communication refactor. Executor's plan.md becomes a thin execution delta (no restating task.md content); Executor runs a deviation self-check before implementing. Universal Lead plan-review gate removed — replaced by ADVICE channel with four cases (complicated / deep-reasoning / knowledge / deviation). Affects: templates/plan.md + new templates/task.md, planning-framework stage-2/4, debug-mode + doc-code-verification-mode stage-4, plan-execution SKILL + all phase references + new task-team-startup.md, task-executor/code-review/task-tester/project-manager agents, plan-status-sync, migrate claude-md-template, plan-status-format reference, help skill, docs site (plan-execution.ejs + feature-planning.ejs).

actions: For each plan in documentation/plans/ that has a README.md containing `### Task N:` headings with embedded per-task fields (Description, Product context, Files, Patterns, Success criteria, Dependencies), split each task section out into `documentation/plans/{plan}/tasks/task-N/task.md` using `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/task.md` as the template. Rewrite the README to contain only plan-level content + a flat task heading index (`### Task N: {Title} <!-- status:pending -->` followed by `- [ ] **Complete**`).

For each newly-created task.md, populate the **Research:** section by scanning the plan's old Tech Stack list and mapping each entry to `documentation/technology/research/libraries/{lib}.md` if that file exists. If the research file doesn't exist, write `None applicable` — Lead's pre-spawn knowledge review will fill real gaps at execution time via `/uc:research`.
Skip plans where `tasks/task-N/task.md` already exists — migration is idempotent.

Completed plans (with operational-report.md or plan.json status `completed`) are safe to migrate — they just get a cleaner structure. In-progress plans will pick up the new structure automatically on their next `/uc:plan-execution` resume via the legacy-plan self-heal in phase-1-setup §1.1.

The CHANGELOG migration action is idempotent: running it twice is safe. Plans created by `/uc:roadmap` as stubs have no embedded per-task content yet, so they're a no-op.

summary: /uc:research now handles Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic API questions natively. Auto-classify treats any topic mentioning `claude code`, `claude agent sdk`, `anthropic api/sdk`, or Claude Code primitives (hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, sub-agents, output styles, plugins, settings, tool use, prompt caching) as `library` mode. The library-mode reference now instructs the researcher to query Ref.tools AND fetch the curated `docs.claude.com` URL roots (`/en/docs/claude-code/`, `/en/api/`, `/en/api/agent-sdk/`) in parallel via WebSearch+WebFetch, merge both, and surface any discrepancies. This avoids needing the built-in `claude-code-guide` agent (which subagents can't spawn anyway) while keeping the same cache/index/file-format pipeline as every other research topic. Help skill description updated to reflect Claude/Anthropic coverage.

The daemon classified any pane whose label started with `knowledge` into a dedicated `tkPane` slot and placed it in the left column below PM — leftover from the removed Tech Knowledge teammate. With /uc:research replacing the knowledge teammate entirely, that code path is unreachable, so it's deleted: `classifyPanes` no longer sets `tkPane`, `computeTargetColumns` builds the left column from `[main, pm]` only, and the log summary drops the `tk` marker. No behavior change for any current label; purely dead-code removal.

Plan-execution Lead-as-Sage refactor (Task 2 of plan 041): remove the shared Tech Knowledge teammate, make Lead the team's knowledge broker via the /uc:research skill. Rewrites skills/plan-execution/SKILL.md's principle from a blanket 'all delegation through teammates' rule into a typed distinction between Teammates (TeamCreate, persistent, stateful, team-graph-tracked — Executor/Reviewer/Tester/PM) and Subagents (Task tool, stateless, one-shot, invisible to team graph — currently the researcher agent). Phase 1.8 now spawns only the PM teammate, then loops /uc:research over the plan's Tech Stack and writes a Knowledge Brief to shared/knowledge-brief.md. The brief is embedded in every executor/reviewer/tester spawn prompt — teammates read it first and fall back to sending QUERY: messages to Lead for anything not covered. Lead answers via /uc:research (cache hit = free, cache miss = one Task-tool subagent spawn), replies ANSWER:, and broadcasts KNOWLEDGE UPDATE: snippets only when new info is broadly relevant across tasks. Phase 5 completion removes the Tech Knowledge shutdown step. Rewires task-executor.md, code-review.md, task-tester.md, project-manager.md (removes knowledge- grid row + SPAWNED knowledge-* event handler). Updates all docs/views/*.ejs pages (index, getting-started, reference, context, plan-execution, setup, feature-planning, token-efficiency, standards, discovery) to describe the new Lead-as-Sage model. Help skill entry for Task Executor updated to describe Knowledge Brief + QUERY routing. Depends on the previous commit (plan 041, Task 1) which introduced /uc:research and the researcher agent.

Unified research (Task 1 of plan 041): replace the split tech-research skill, Tech Knowledge agent, and Market Analyzer agent with a single cache-first `/uc:research` skill fronting a stateless `researcher` subagent. Research findings become first-class project documentation under `documentation/technology/research/{libraries,patterns}/` (new) with frontmatter-driven per-entry staleness — library docs default to 10 days, patterns to 90 days, market snapshots to 30 days, and historical/retrospective research freezes (expires:null). Market research continues to go to `documentation/product/research/` unchanged. A machine-maintained `index.json` (written atomically by the researcher, queried via jq by the skill) drives fast cache-hit lookups with zero agent spawn on hits. The skill auto-classifies query mode (library/patterns/market) with signal heuristics; ambiguous queries ask via AskUserQuestion. Progressive disclosure: `agents/researcher.md` holds spawn protocol + file format + io-protocol inline, and one of three mode-specific references (`skills/research/references/{library,patterns,market}-mode.md`) is read per call. `skills/docs-manager/` gains a new `references/technology-research.md` and routing-table/layout updates so research files are a first-class citizen of the canonical documentation structure. Plan-execution refactor (Task 2 — Lead-as-Sage, typed teammate-vs-subagent distinction, executor/reviewer/tester rewiring, docs/views/*.ejs) ships in a follow-up commit.

/uc:chrome-debug gains a multi-account failure mode: browser/Claude Code account mismatch. The bridge (wss://bridge.claudeusercontent.com) pairs Claude Code and the Claude-in-Chrome extension by matching Anthropic account identities on both ends — when Claude Code is authenticated as account X but the browser is logged into account Y, pairing silently fails and symptoms look like transport-layer problems (empty tabs_context_mcp, intermittent timeouts) that no amount of native-host restarting will fix. New Step 3b preflight asks the user to confirm account match before running transport diagnostics, skipped automatically in single-account setups. New Known Failure Mode entry captures the full symptom/cause/check/fix cycle with `claude auth status` as the Claude Code side check and claude.ai account menu as the browser side check. Machine-specific profile-management commands (e.g., profiled-claude on the reference machine) are delegated to ~/.claude/skills/machine-context/claude-profiles.md, keeping the marketplace skill portable. Help skill entry unchanged (the skill's purpose statement still captures this).

/uc:setup now checks whether the `ultraclaude-agent` npm package is installed and, if so, compares the installed version against the latest published on npm. When outdated, setup surfaces the gap in its status table and offers to run `npm update -g ultraclaude-agent` as part of the fix-missing-prerequisites flow (step 5.9). Never auto-installs the agent — installation remains a deliberate user choice. This closes a gap where users who installed the agent once and never ran `npm update` would miss every subsequent bug fix (including the project-path-with-spaces fix that blocks project discovery for any path containing a space). The npm lookup uses a 5-second timeout so offline/slow registries never stall setup. Marker file `~/.claude/ultra/uc-setup.json` now records the installed agent version (or null). Docs site `docs/views/docs/setup.ejs` mentions the new behavior. Help skill entry for /uc:setup updated with the new sentence.

Project Manager: explicit Lead label sanity check on every verification pass. PM now counts how many panes in the window carry `main-context` via `grep -cx`, interprets the count (1=healthy, 0=broken, 2+=duplicate), and self-heals the 0-case by relabeling the Lead pane back to the canonical `main-context`. Catches downstream drift where a project customization writes a non-canonical label like `lead-*` — the tmux layout daemon only anchors windows on `main-context`, so a wrong label silently stops the team grid from updating. PM also logs the incident in its operational report so the Lead can investigate where the bad label came from.

Restore pipelined successor pre-spawn and move the lazy-tester signal earlier in plan execution. Executor now sends `Task {N} code complete — writing impl report` to Lead *before* writing `impl.md` or committing; Lead lazy-spawns `tester-{N}` on that signal so the Tester cold-reads plan/product/testing docs in parallel with the Executor finishing the impl report. The same signal triggers pipeline pre-spawn: if a concurrency slot is free and there is a pending task whose only remaining blocker is task N, Lead pre-spawns that successor's Executor + Reviewer with a Pipeline-mode block in the spawn prompt. The pre-spawned Executor runs through steps 1–3.7 normally (codebase research, plan, Lead plan review) and then parks at a new step 3.9 wait gate, sending `Task {M} planning complete — awaiting implementation approval` to Lead. When the predecessor reaches `task done`, Lead sends `Implementation approved — predecessor task {N} passed all stages. Proceed to implement.` and the parked Executor runs 3.5/4/5/6 normally. At most one pre-spawn per `code complete` event; parked state is not persisted in checkpoints (pipeline is a latency optimization, not a correctness guarantee); on predecessor escalation the parked successor stays alive unless the user aborts. Updates: skills/plan-execution/SKILL.md (message handler table + flow diagram + key principles + Lead Behavior + Communication Protocol), references/phase-1-setup.md (no-pipeline note replaced), references/phase-2-spawn-prompts.md (conditional Pipeline-mode block for executor spawn), references/phase-4-failure-handling.md (pipeline-spawned successors section), agents/task-executor.md (new step 3.9 wait gate + rewritten step 4.5 earlier signal), agents/project-manager.md ((pipeline) SPAWNED variant), docs/views/docs/plan-execution.ejs (restored pre-spawn description in flow + concurrency paragraph), skills/help/SKILL.md (plan-execution 3-sentence description). Roadmap stub scaffolder now writes "stub" (was "pending"); stage-4 approval gate writes "approved" (was "pending"); plan-status-format reference table updated to list the new plan enum. plan-status-sync inference rules and status mapping updated to emit the new values and alias legacy plan-level "pending" → "approved" on read. templates/plan.md header now lists Stub as a valid status so plans upgraded from roadmap stubs render correctly. summary: Add /uc:chrome-debug skill (portable Claude-in-Chrome diagnostics: stale native host, service worker idle, bridge race, profile-scoped manifest, switch_browser naming prompt) and extend /uc:setup with optional machine-context scaffolding. The chrome-debug skill reads per-machine values from ~/.claude/skills/machine-context/chrome-debug.md when present (primary Chrome install, dual-browser setup, VM-to-host routing, paths, extension ID) and falls back to runtime detection via $HOME/whoami/jq otherwise. /uc:setup step 5.9 creates ~/.claude/skills/machine-context/ interactively with 6 topic files (environment, chrome-debug, claude-profiles, development, network, warnings) via the new references/machine-context-interview.md procedure; idempotent and non-clobbering on rerun. summary: task-tester: invoke /chrome-debug before falling back to code-level verification on mcp__claude-in-chrome__* failures. Plan 003 and plan 009 both saw testers give up after 3-4 browser failures and revert to code-level analysis, when a 30-second chrome-debug run would have auto-recovered the connection in most cases (stale native host, suspended service worker, bridge race). The task-tester agent now invokes chrome-debug as the first recourse, escalates to PM/user only if chrome-debug cannot recover, and falls back to code-level verification only after both attempts. Aligns with chrome-debug s existing autonomous auto-recovery operating mode. NOTE: this commit references /chrome-debug (personal namespace); the follow-up in seq 114 corrects it to the plugin-namespaced /uc:chrome-debug once chrome-debug itself moved into the marketplace.

Drop elapsed_seconds from plan.json. The field is fully derivable from started_at and ended_at (or now() for in-progress rows), and the Ultra Claude Dashboard now computes elapsed at read time. Project Manager no longer writes elapsed_seconds on monitoring ticks, stage-done events, or execution-complete — removing the only reason the cron tick needed to touch plan.json every 5 minutes when nothing else was happening. plan-status-format reference updated to drop the field from all examples. Existing plan.json files that still contain elapsed_seconds are harmless; the dashboard ingestion silently ignores the field.

migration.precondition: Project has documentation/plans/*/plan.json files (any Ultra Claude project that has executed a plan).
migration.actions: No action required. Existing plan.json files may still contain elapsed_seconds at plan, task, or stage level; the Ultra Claude Dashboard now ignores the field on ingest and computes elapsed from started_at/ended_at. New plan executions will omit the field automatically. If you want to tidy existing plan.json files, delete any elapsed_seconds keys by hand — but it is optional and purely cosmetic.
migration.conflicts: None. Removal is backward-compatible: the field is dropped, not renamed, so nothing reads it. Dashboards on older versions that still reference the field will simply see no updates to it — elapsed badges there will freeze at the last written value until the dashboard is upgraded.

summary: Tmux layout daemon: replace break-pane/join-pane/resize-pane rearrangement with atomic select-layout. Each tick computes the target column layout, derives a TAILQ permutation via swap-pane (cheap pointer swaps, no layout re-flow), then applies a precomputed layout string (with layout_checksum reproduced in JS from tmux/layout-custom.c) in a single select-layout call. The whole arrange is one batched tmux invocation with exactly one redraw — sub-10ms regardless of pane count, effectively eliminating visible pane tearing. Daemon also sorts task-column members deterministically by role: executor (top), reviewer (middle), tester (bottom). Agents task-executor, code-review, and task-tester now self-label as `task-N-executor`, `task-N-reviewer`, `task-N-tester` respectively; legacy `task-N` labels (no role suffix) still classify correctly and sort after role-labeled siblings for backward compatibility. Project Manager documentation updated with the new label table.

Tmux layout daemon: fold unlabeled/unnamed panes into the rightmost task column (up to 3 panes per task team) instead of giving them their own column, so teammates spawning into an existing task land in the correct column from the start. Replace label-based change detection with a target-layout signature so labeling a pane that doesn't change the resulting column assignment no longer triggers a redundant break-pane/join-pane cycle (reduces visible pane-tearing). Drop the post-arrange re-scan. Tighten poll interval from 2000ms to 1000ms for snappier reaction to new agent spawns.

Restructure plan-enhancer skill into a pure reference library at references/planning-framework/. Each planning mode (feature-mode, debug-mode, doc-code-verification-mode) now has its own per-stage reference files (references/stage-{1..4}.md) that progressively import the framework counterparts as the model transitions into each stage. Mode SKILL.md files are lean — they read framework.md once at activation, then point to stage-1.md with an explicit anti-preload rule. Existing-plan handling lives in framework.md with mode extensions in stage-1.md (feature-mode keeps stub-plan detection there). Help skill and docs site updated to surface the planning framework as a reference library, not a skill. Migrate skill no longer reads plan-enhancer (it ran its own simpler approve/execute flow).

Lower PM agent usage-pause threshold from 85% to 80% for earlier proactive pausing when extra_usage is disabled.

Fix statusline to normalize resets_at as epoch integers. Claude Code sometimes sends ISO strings which failed Zod validation (z.number().int()) on the server, causing 422 rejections that blocked all usage sync.

Fix statusline overwrite guard (most-recent-write-wins replaces keep-higher-value), add source_session_id traceability, enrich session files with pid/tmux_pane/last_activity, add /uc:session-cleanup skill for stale session management.

Fix team shutdown race condition: executor now collects explicit READY TO EXIT confirmations from both reviewer and tester before reporting task done to Lead, preventing premature team shutdown while tester is still working.
